headline: Trump shifts to economic pressure on Iran as Hormuz talks stall on US concessions
summary: President Trump said Washington is 'low-keying it' with Iran and relying on sanctions and a naval blockade rather than new strikes, describing the US as 'only semi-negotiating' with Tehran. Oil prices ticked up as Iran's Revolutionary Guards said the Strait of Hormuz would not reopen until the US lifts the blockade, ends military action, and pays war reparations — conditions Washington has not accepted. Iran and Oman said talks on new shipping-lane coordinates had reached their 'final' stages but a broader deal remains conditional on those US concessions.

summary: A Ukrainian drone attack on the city of Nizhnekamsk in Russia's Tatarstan region killed at least 13 people, including one child, and wounded dozens more, Russian officials said. Ukraine's armed forces confirmed the Taneko oil refinery was struck; Ukrainian defence manufacturer FirePoint said its FP-1 drones were used. headline: Typhoon Dolphin forces evacuation of more than one million in eastern China; nearly 1,000 Shanghai flights cancelled
summary: Typhoon Dolphin made landfall in Zhejiang province with maximum winds of 150 km/h, prompting the evacuation of more than one million people and the cancellation of nearly 1,000 flights in Shanghai. Wenzhou alone relocated roughly 900,000 residents and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters; forecasters warned of 250–500 mm of rain in parts of Zhejiang, raising the risk of flooding and landslides. A nine-year-old boy from Wenling was reported missing after being swept into the sea. The storm had already caused eight deaths in the Philippines and injuries in Japan's Okinawa.

summary: A Damascus court convicted ousted leader Bashar al-Assad and sentenced him to death in absentia on Tuesday, finding him guilty of premeditated murder, torture, and crimes against humanity committed during Syria's civil war. Iran's Supreme National Security Council demands the US pay war compensation, lift sanctions and the blockade, and unfreeze Iranian assets before reopening; Trump said the US has "total control" and is betting on economic pressure. Shipping data firm Kpler recorded only 14 ships crossing the strait on Tuesday, compared with roughly 130 per day before the war.

headline: Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan activate Mecca pact's joint defence structure
summary: Turkey's defence ministry announced on Thursday that Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan will form joint political and military coordination mechanisms under the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement signed on August 7, including defence ministers, foreign ministers, and military chiefs, with joint exercises and defence industry cooperation also planned. Turkey's President Erdogan said he hopes more countries will join the pact, which stipulates that an armed attack on any member would be treated as an attack on all — similar to NATO's Article 5 — though Turkey's foreign minister stressed it is not directed against Iran or any other country. Analysts described the pact as far short of a true NATO-style alliance because of diverging strategic interests.

headline: Iran-US war pushes Iraq to the brink of a state payroll crisis
summary: Iraqi oil exports fell roughly 83% in March compared with a year earlier after Iran blocked the Strait of Hormuz, and by May seaborne crude exports were down 97%, slashing government revenue to between $2 billion and $2.3 billion a month — far below the $6.5 billion to $8.2 billion needed each month to pay public sector workers, pensioners, and welfare recipients. University and ministry employees have already begun protesting delayed salaries, and the government's estimated $83 billion in reserves is projected to cover only 10 to 11 months of salary payments. A UK advisory firm estimated Hormuz traffic is unlikely to return to normal levels until at least 2028.

headline: Ebola on track to surpass 2014–16 death toll as health workers reach only 30% of cases
summary: The WHO director-general said Thursday that the 2026 Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, declared on May 15, has caused more than 2,000 deaths and at least 4,300 cases, and is on pace to exceed the deadliest outbreak ever — the 2014–16 epidemic that killed at least 11,000 people. The current outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo species of Ebola, for which no approved vaccine or treatment exists; ongoing regional instability means health workers are reaching only about 30% of cases. The UK's medicines regulator has cleared the first human trials of a Bundibugyo vaccine developed by Oxford researchers.

Arday had become Cambridge's youngest Black professor in 2023 and denied the plagiarism allegations, saying in his resignation letter that 'the relentless accusations, speculation and public commentary have taken a profound toll.' summary: Bangladesh's parliament voted Thursday to elect a new president, with the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party's candidate Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, 78, widely expected to prevail over retired Colonel Oli Ahmad, nominee of the Jamaat-e-Islami-led opposition alliance. headline: Bangladesh elects BNP veteran Alamgir as president in first contested race since 1991
summary: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, 78, of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party was elected president on August 20, receiving 255 parliamentary votes against 88 for his rival Oli Ahmad. headline: Six months into Iran war, Hormuz traffic at a fraction of pre-war levels with 6,000 sailors stranded
summary: Commodity carrier traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has averaged 15 transits per day since hostilities resumed on July 8 — down from a pre-war daily average of 95 — with two-thirds of transits now 'dark', meaning vessels have disabled transponders or otherwise obscured their routes, according to maritime tracker Kpler. Some 6,000 sailors and 500 ships remain stuck in the Gulf, and at least 20 sailors and dockworkers have been killed in incidents since the war began. Countries affected by conflicts in 2026 — including Iran, Russia, Libya and Venezuela — together produce roughly 43% of global oil supply, Reuters calculations show, with the current Gulf disruption running at an estimated 5 to 7 million barrels per day.

headline: Russian AI-guided drone killed three civilians in Zaporizhzhia, Ukrainian analysis finds
summary: Ukrainian drone experts, military commanders and a forensic team that examined wreckage determined that a Russian drone which killed three people in Zaporizhzhia in July was guided by an autonomous AI system based on an Nvidia Jetson Orin module, not a human pilot. summary: After talks in Geneva mediated by Switzerland, the Democratic Republic of Congo government and the Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 rebel group agreed on a roadmap for peace negotiations, backed by the US, Qatar, the African Union and Switzerland. Simultaneously, Iran-backed Houthis struck a crude oil tanker in the Red Sea off Saudi Arabia and attacked the port city of Mokha, threatening the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which Gulf exporters had been using as an alternative to the Hormuz route.

headline: Glacial collapse kills at least 270 and leaves more than 1,300 missing on Nepal-Tibet border

Dozens of bridges and roughly 40km of road were destroyed, hampering rescue operations; Nepal army helicopters airlifted more than 100 survivors and some foreign nationals to Kathmandu.
